text:
marta: Heads-up: onboarding marigold-9b (community checkpoint). Legal flagged a clause that mentions 'derivative binaries' and a commercial redistribution prohibition. Can we offer a quantized 4-bit serve-only variant behind Dedicated without exposing binaries? :wave:

devin: Can you paste the exact license language? small differences matter. :mag:

marta: Sure, copied from LICENSE: ```
Redistribution: The model weights and any derivative binary artifacts (including quantized weight files and optimized kernels) may not be redistributed for commercial use. Hosting the model to provide API inference is allowed provided the model binaries are not publicly distributed. Attribution: Any product use must credit the Original Authors and include a link to the LICENSE.
```

piotr: Short ops take: serving via API should be fine if we never expose the binaries. The trouble is Dedicated customer-hosted where they request mounted volumes or file access 1 that could be redistribution. We should block downloads and add export denial in the pipeline.

rachel: ML experiments: ran 4-bit GPTQ on gpu-dev. Latency ~2.3x, MMLU down ~1.4 pts, Rouge-L -1.0, safety classifier FPR +0.5. Not ideal but within our usual quant tradeoffs. I can run the full eval suite if legal confirms serve-only is acceptable.

legal: Quick read from counsel: "Serving via API is permitted under this wording as long as derivative binaries (including quantized files) are not redistributed. For Dedicated deployments where customers receive binaries, require an explicit license exception or deny binary access. Attribution requirement is acceptable; record compliance steps." :white_check_mark:

artifact-bot: Ingest scan: marigold-9b artifacts uploaded to s3://models/internal/marigold-9b/2026-03-24/; detected fp16 tarball; no quant artifacts present. License tag: MGO-1. Public ACL: false.

devin: Action items while we wait on formal memo: 1) Piotr - add ingest hook to deny export when metadata.license=="MGO-1"; 2) Rachel - run full eval suite (MMLU, HellaSwag, summarization, safety/regressions) and attach diffs; 3) Marta - draft attribution text and provenance header.

piotr: I'll open the PR for the export block and audit logging. We can also encrypt storage of artifacts and restrict roles that can access the raw tar.gz. PR shortly.

rachel: Uploaded quick eval diffs: https://artifacts.internal/marigold-9b/quant-eval-2026-03-24.csv 1 MMLU: base 63.1 -> 61.7, HellaSwag 87.0 -> 86.0, Rouge-L -1.0, Safety FPR +0.5. I'll add prompt-level failure cases in the full run.

marta: Draft attribution: "Marigold-9B 1 Marigold Research Collective. Licensed under MGO-1. See LICENSE." Proposed provenance header: `X-Model-Origin: marigold-9b;license=MGO-1;quantized=4bit;artifact=2026-03-24`. Posting to docs for review.

ops-bot: Scheduled scrub job for any public quant artifacts under s3://models/internal/marigold-9b/2026-03-24/ if discovered. Audit log will record any access attempts.

marta: Thanks all. Once Piotr's PR lands and legal posts the signed memo we'll proceed with internal canary: Hosted + Dedicated serve-only (no binary export), include attribution in product docs, and offer fp16 fallback route for sensitive endpoints. Leaving thread open until canary RFC merged. :tada:
